mission.title: Five Are Fallen
mission.description: Find the site where E Pluribus Neo rescued Lock, through EPN systems and the black market.

npc.say: Oh crap! It was the Machines in our system!

No, we did not contradict the terrorist story of Sentinels at the site earlier, as there was no need. The less they know of our actual movements, the better, yes? The transfer of Lock to New Zion has in all likelihood helped to spread this misinformation among the Zionites.
"Emotion" and "hope" are frequent excuses among humans for failure to observe facts.

phase.briefing:
Operative, we were on the verge of taking over E Pluribus Neo scanning systems around Zion's old city which, in conjunction with our own scans, would have allowed us to triangulate the suspected Mauser's transmission source quickly, but the circumvented EPN security systems inexplicably reactivated, using a variant of their previous algorithm, which resisted all attempts to break it.
While this endeavor on the surface of the planet has not been successful, it is possible that we can penetrate those scanning systems from EPN computers within the Matrix. Such computers have been isolated at the location you see indicated.

enter.say: Since this is supposed to be an EPN playpen, those signals I'm reading in there are probably the cultists and their computers.

done.say:
What the hey? Mismatch? It's their own damn system! Did we hijack EPN's reject squad?
Gonna have to talk to Gray about this...

phase.briefing:
That issue is beyond my capacity to handle. It has been referred to the appropriate parties.
Hm... There is a related problem that may be more appropriate to our particular capabilities, {player}. I will have Agent Pace present the pertinent data to you.

enter.say: Some of our programs in there...and no EPN, at least.

talk.say:
That is a recording of a typical Pluribus Neo account of Mauser's demise. You have noted the obvious shortcomings in the story, yes? *Prima*, Lock did not see the Sentinels himself, and we certainly have no record of our Sentinels killing Mauser. *Secondo*, Lock did not actually claim to see Mauser killed.
Later accounts by EPN described the building in which they found Lock as roughly above Zion, with Sentinel claw marks around an opening torn in the outer wall; but they found no Sentinel wreckage, and only blood and fingerprints--no body--of Mauser: curious details and omissions. You see that it has become important for us to inspect this building for ourselves.

objective.text: Kill the E Pluribus Neo Fighter

phase.briefing:
As accessing data from Pluribus Neo systems has proven momentarily...inefficient, we will seek data on their recorded location of Lock's rescue point from another source.
In this case, the information in question--the coordinates of a derelict and wrecked facility on the Earth's surface--although possibly a topic of some interest to pro-Zionite humans, would likely not have been marked as highly classified. It is almost certain to have made its way into the realm of black-market information dealers. This is an area that we monitor but do not usually interfere with directly, as, left undisturbed, it constitutes a useful source of information on illicit activities.
For this reason, we will have you access this loose network via a third party.

enter.say:
Aubrey Casca is an addict of the net's back channels. He's spent a fortune on access to just about every site your mom would have told you not to go to, if she'd known about them. The Machines have enough cyber crime evidence on him to put him away for life, but it looks like they've opted for a solution that won't place another burden on the simulation's prison system.
Uh... Oh, yeah. Gray suggested to me that we use a silencer for this, just in case Casca has nosy neighbors.

talk.say: Aah! No no-- I didn't... Yes, all right, I did claim mail fraud on the newsgroup just to throw a smokescreen up in front of the credit fraud...but...look... I'll-- I'll make it up to you! Do you need another account? I've got dozens! Clean records, great ratings--everything you could want!

done.say: Let's help ourselves to his computer.

Ew. I feel so dirty...
If that seller was legit...relatively speaking...then all we gotta do is make the pickup.

phase.briefing: The seller insisted on a face-to-face transaction. You will be provided with an account containing the necessary funds.

enter.say:
You're supposed to meet the seller's courier in there. As far as they know, you're Casca's courier. Should be an uneventful hand-off; never know with these types though.
I'm...not getting much in there. I think they've got scan suppression running. Figures.

talk.say:
I'll just be takin' a minute to check that.
... All right, mon. I tink we can do business. Check the computa there.

done.say: I just got an activity reading from the terminal in there.

objective.text: Get the data from the computer

done.say: Looks like our cash was good. No problem found with that data. Get it to a hardline and we'll see what the Machines make of it.

objective.text: Upload the data at a hardline

mission.finish:
The data identified, via images and positional data, the building in which Lock was found as the same lab where, previously, the renegade scientist Danielle Wright was terminated by our Sentinels. The terrorists had not known this lab's location, thus, it is unlikely that this coincidence is a fabrication.
It could explain some of Mauser's demonstrated capabilities. Wright specialized in biological interfaces and broadcast technology. We had thought all data and equipment in the lab destroyed at the time of Wright's termination, but it is possible that Mauser, who records indicate was a highly skilled technician, could have located or salvaged some of her technology.
Thank you, {player}. Based on this information, we are modifying our search for his broadcast source to cover the area between the lab and the general area to which his signal was traced previously.
